# Table 11: RQ4 telemetry ablation (H4b)

RE2, oracle alert, no shift, the named sources dropped before ingest, in 04 §5.2 order. H4b reads AC@1 among CONFIRMED in every cell. CONFIRMED verdicts is derived, not read: it is answer_rate_confirmed × n_fault of summary.json's selective_accuracy entry, rounded to the integer k, and the generator stops unless that product is within 1e-6 of k (a k / n check, 03 §13.3), so it is the exact count behind the rate, not a new statistic. re2-oracle-rq1-v1 and re2-oracle-rq3-off-v1 do not list selective_accuracy, so no unperturbed row has a selective-accuracy value. The none point is re2-oracle-rq1-v1, whose verdicts are uncalibrated (split none); the none rows of re2-oracle-rq3-v1 (revised as re2-oracle-rq3-off-v1) are the calibrated unperturbed reference for coverage and set size, since every perturbed run reuses its calibration files (04 §5.4 item 4). 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals in brackets; a value without one says so (04 §8); failed, timed-out, no-alert, rejected and unranked runs count as misses. Outcomes counts all the group's rows per run outcome (03 §13.3): its fault-case runs and, in an experiment with normal windows, one row per normal window, so it can exceed Fault-case runs. Avg@5, MRR, Fine AC@k and Rerank@1 are listed by these experiments and are in each one's summary.json, but not tabulated here. Protocol of each experiment: see Sources.
